newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia sees 1996/97 oil price at $20/barrel.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia sees 1996/97 oil price at $20/barrel.

text.p: Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana said on Wednesday he expected Indonesian oil prices to average $20 a barrel in fiscal 1996/97 (April-March).
"There is a possibility that Indonesian oil prices will average $20 a barrel from April to March next year. Oil prices are currently stable," he told reporters.
The price of Indonesia's main Minas crude oil for October lifting was calculated at $23.12 per barrel, up $2.10 from September, traders in Tokyo said on November 1.
Sudjana reaffirmed that Indonesia wanted the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) to maintain its output ceiling of 25.033 million barrels per day (bpd).
OPEC ministers will gather in Vienna later this month to discuss members' quotas and oil price developments.

"We want OPEC to keep its current output ceiling to stabilise oil prices. We want the ceiling to be maintained, if possible, for one year because if we raise the ceiling it will have a negative impact on prices," he said.
